meta.title: FLIP THE FUNNEL: How to Use Existing Customers to Gain New Ones
meta.author: Joseph Jaffe

sentences: In the **Foreword** of Joseph Jaffe's "Flip the Funnel," the author criticizes how companies handle **customer service** today, turning it into a cost-cutting "church of churn" instead of an opportunity to build **customer loyalty**.
The societal shift towards **transparency** and **authenticity** makes old practices obsolete as consumers get honest feedback online, shifting power away from traditional marketing.

Jaffe argues for turning **customer experiences** into the new focus of acquisition strategies, equating customer service with **marketing** and using real-world examples to highlight successful customer engagement strategies.
In today's **dynamic world**, many **traditional marketing concepts** like S.T.P.
(Segmenting, Targeting, Positioning) and the **Four Ps** (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) are becoming outdated.
This text urges readers to rethink these **conventional strategies** and adopt a new model focused on **Content, Commerce, Community, Context, Customization, and Conversation**.
The **old marketing funnel** - A.I.D.A (Awareness, Interest, Desire, Action) - is being challenged because it no longer reflects **contemporary consumer behavior**.
Instead of being linear and predictable, customer journeys are now **non-linear**, filled with **involvement, empowerment, and demonstration**.

parts.title: Shifts in Business Strategy: From Expansion to Customer Centricity

sentences: In recent times, the downfall of many companies stems from ignoring **customer** needs, focusing instead on **expansion**, and emphasizing **diversification** and **acquisitions**.
When considering companies that have folded, many lacked **customer referral** programs or neglected to prioritize **customer service** and loyalty.
A notable example is **Starbucks**, which lost sight of its core values by prioritizing breadth over depth, thereby alienating customers who perceived their offerings as too **expensive**.
Marketing efforts such as defensive ad campaigns further illustrate companies losing their edge in the **trust** stakes.
A shift in strategy is needed, from prioritizing **acquisition** to enhancing **customer experience** and **loyalty**.
**IBM** makes it **easy** for customers to **contact** them through **multiple channels** like email, **toll-free lines**, **live chat**, and even **virtual world** meet-ups.
This **humanizes** the technology space and enhances interactions.
Conversely, **Microsoft** is criticized for its **confusing support** system, which often places the **onus** on customers to solve issues themselves.
This highlights the **importance** of technology in **improving** relationships rather than just being seen as a **cost-saving tool**.
The importance of **commitment** and **follow-through** in customer service is emphasized by a positive example involving Audi, where they ensured their customer was satisfied after a service visit.

This kind of attention can lead to **repeat business** and **word-of-mouth referrals**.Even though **reminders** may seem unnecessary, they help customers keep track of appointments or key dates, acknowledging their **busy lives** and reinforcing their connection to the brand.
Businesses are encouraged to engage customers without assuming constant **top-of-mind awareness**.
Obama's campaign leveraged **social media** effectively, creating a vast **online presence** and utilizing platforms like MyBO to centralize activities.
This approach allowed for **ongoing dialogues** through various content forms such as blogs, podcasts, and videos, establishing credibility with **influential audiences**.
The intention was to create a movement driven by **hope and change**, encapsulated in the slogan "Yes We Can."
This sentiment was a **powerful incentive** for participation, making the campaign feel more like a movement than an election, thereby engaging people on a deeper emotional level.
Companies should have a holistic approach to **customer experience** that blends existing **service techniques** and **innovation** to continuously add value.
It is essential to prioritize **customer loyalty** and avoid creating hard-to-navigate **loyalty programs** that frustrate customers with conditions like **blackouts**.
Businesses must avoid making it easy for competitors to outshine them through authentic, customer-friendly policies.

parts.title: Customer Service: A Strategic Driver and Differentiator

sentences: **Customer service** is a **strategic driver** that needs to be at the **forefront** of business strategy.
It should join the ranks of **strategic planning, marketing** and **branding**.
It is vital for creating unique **competitive advantages** and can be a **major differentiator** from competitors.
Organizations must shift from viewing customer service as a **cost** and instead treat it as a **sound investment**.

This change requires overhauling **recruitment, training, empowerment**, and **compensation** of staff responsible for customer service, emphasizing the importance of not outsourcing these crucial functions and keeping them central to the **company’s core**.

parts.title: Navigating Virtual Worlds and Integrated Service

sentences: **Virtual Worlds Defined:** The text expands on the definition of virtual worlds as environments where people interact through avatars or profiles, maintaining anonymity.
**Challenge:** Companies face a dual challenge to deploy responsive capabilities in the **"third dimension"**—the blend of physical, digital, and virtual worlds—and interconnect these environments.

**Service Across Dimensions:** Emphasis is placed on the need for **integrated systems** that document all customer interactions and enhance the consistency and quality of customer service across various platforms.

parts.title: Empowering Consumer-Driven Solutions and Community Interaction

sentences: **Method's Co-founders** initiated **user-driven content** by partnering with **Get Satisfaction**, empowering their **consumers** to **modify** and **curate** brand-related questions.
This **crowdsourcing** is akin to **consumer-generated content** meeting brand-oriented **community interaction**.
It's about recognizing that **no one knows the brand** better than the **customers** themselves, emphasizing **collaboration** to unlock new potential while **resonating with communities**.

An example highlights the **potential of crowdsourced solutions**: updating an iPhone and later finding apps missing led to a **community-driven solution** found through **social media** rather than official customer service; demonstrating how community can effectively provide solutions faster.

**Social media criticism** noted it wasn't optimally enabling brands, hinting that the true strength of social media lies in **retention** rather than **acquisition**—consumers prefer **genuine dialogues** with other **consumers** over interactions with brands or products.

parts.title: The Shift in Consumer Trust and Influence

sentences: When shopping online, many rely on Google rankings, which do not differentiate between big corporations and individual blogs.
For spontaneous buying decisions, people often turn to platforms like Twitter, trusting strangers' opinions due to a general faith in collective wisdom until they experience disappointment.
Consequently, corporations no longer hold the power to control consumer purchasing behavior.
The best hope for companies is to rely on their customers to advocate for their products' worth.
Increasingly, without solicitation, customers are engaging in recommending goods to others, particularly through blogging platforms.
These points highlight the need for companies to leverage consumer-generated content to maintain influence and foster customer pride in association with their brand.
Consumers trust peer recommendations more than marketing, which is crucial as bloggers and social media users voluntarily share experiences.
Companies should strategize on engaging consumer advocates rather than rely only on traditional advertising.
By fostering genuine relationships with customers, businesses can encourage them to participate in promoting the brand, thus enhancing organic growth through peer-to-peer endorsements.

This organic involvement becomes more significant as more users engage in blogs and online discussions sharing personal insights about products, which companies can harness to influence future purchases positively.
Meanwhile, brands must acknowledge the tangible and social currency value of referrals and align marketing strategies to emphasize authenticity and trustworthiness.

parts.title: Flipping the Corporate Funnel to Focus on Customer Experience

sentences: Flipping the funnel involves **embracing change** within a company's culture, enhancing **customer centric strategies** by aligning retention and acquisition efforts.
This change demands an organizational overhaul, focusing on **customer experience** rather than solely acquisition.

Companies often get stuck between **strategic and tactical phases** in adopting customer-centric approaches, so a common entry point, usually **strategic planning**, is crucial for evolving and integrating corporate strategies effectively.
In this context, questions arise about **who should own the customer relationship** - marketing, customer service, or an emerging entity such as a **Chief Experience Officer**.
Different roles are suggested for different stages of organizational integration, from tactical customer services to a strategic CMO or holistic approaches.

Building consensus and **measuring success** are pivotal in transitioning into a customer-experience-centric culture, driving home the importance of **integrated roles and continuous support across all organization levels**.

parts.title: Commitment to Change and Customer Centricity

sentences: In a rapidly changing world, **committed change** within an organization is crucial for success.
While some companies simply involve themselves in changes like a chicken in a breakfast, others like **Virgin America or Zappos** make a full commitment like a pig does.
Committing to a new **company culture** or launching a new brand can translate into exceptional customer experiences, which lead to customer evangelism.
It's not just about adding **Wi-Fi on every flight** like Virgin did, but about creating a genuinely engaged community of employees and customers that share **common respect and purpose**.
Commitment to change requires being resource-intensive and **embracing customer feedback** to drive constant improvement.
Virgin America exemplifies this by utilizing real-time feedback from customers to adjust their offerings, from diverse menus to customer service response.
This approach requires a corporate maturity that embeds **customer-centricity at the core of an organization’s DNA**, allowing everyone in the company to own the customer experience.
